record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: The first-order theory 2-RAN lies strictly between CARD(Σ_2) and WPHP(Σ_2). Determine the relationship between GPHP(Σ_2) and 2-RAN: for example, which of these principles implies the other, if either does, and whether they are comparable.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. The first-order theory 2-RAN is between CARD(Σ2) and WPHP(Σ2), but how about GPHP(Σ2) and 2-RAN?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the language of first-order arithmetic. For a class of formulas Γ (in particular Γ = Σ₂), consider the following schemas, each formulated in a base theory of arithmetic that proves induction for bounded formulas (e.g., I∆₀ + exp):

• CARD(Γ): the cardinality scheme asserting, for every Γ-definable relation viewed as a bounded "function" or "set", the standard counting/cardinality axioms (existence and uniqueness of the cardinality of a Γ-definable bounded set, with the usual additivity and bijection-invariance properties).

• WPHP(Γ) (weak pigeonhole principle for Γ): for every Γ-definable function F and every a > 0, F is not a map from 2a into a; equivalently, there is no Γ-definable injection from {0,…,2a−1} into {0,…,a−1}.

• GPHP(Γ) (generalized pigeonhole principle for Γ): for every Γ-definable function F and all a, b with a > b ≥ 1, F is not an injection from {0,…,a−1} into {0,…,b−1}; equivalently, any Γ-definable function from a larger finite initial segment into a smaller one has a collision.

• 2-RAN: the first-order Ramsey-type principle stating that for every Γ-definable 2-coloring of pairs from a sufficiently large finite initial segment of the natural numbers there exists a homogeneous set of prescribed size (the "2-Ramsey" principle restricted to the level Σ₂).

It is known that, over the base theory, 2-RAN strictly implies CARD(Σ₂) and is strictly implied by WPHP(Σ₂); that is,

   WPHP(Σ₂)  ⊋  2-RAN  ⊋  CARD(Σ₂).

Determine the relationship over the base theory between GPHP(Σ₂) and 2-RAN. Specifically: does GPHP(Σ₂) imply 2-RAN, does 2-RAN imply GPHP(Σ₂), are the two principles equivalent, or are they incomparable?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent collection of problems on computability theory and descriptive set theory. A web search for the relationship between GPHP(Σ₂) and 2-RAN over weak arithmetic theories returned no published solution; existing literature discusses WPHP, generalized PHP and Ramsey-type principles but does not settle this specific comparison.

status_evidence.title: Models of Bounded Arithmetic and variants of Pigeonhole Principle
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses WPHP and variants in bounded arithmetic but does not resolve the GPHP(Σ₂) vs 2-RAN comparison.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on PHP variants in bounded arithmetic does not contain a resolution of the GPHP(Σ₂) vs 2-RAN question.

status_evidence.title: Weak Pigeonhole Principle, and Randomized Computation (Jeřábek)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatment of WPHP and related principles over bounded arithmetic; the specific 2-RAN vs GPHP(Σ₂) problem is not addressed.
status_evidence.claim: No known resolution of the comparison appears in the standard references on WPHP.
